So, it took about a day but I was able to get FaceSwap to work, after a fair bit of trial and error. There seems to be quite a lot of assumption in some of the setup instructions about people's technical ability or what's already on their machine, so I'll go through here what worked for me: 1. I'm using FaceSwap in Windows 10. This is a command line utility and not a graphic interface, so you need to type stuff but you can see the error messages better for troubleshooting. 2. I needed to install on Windows: a. Python 3.6 from the Python web site (as noted in most setup instructions). NOTE: The "click here to install" link installs the 32-bit version and doesn't seem to really mention this, you need to scroll down a bit and find the 64 bit version for Windows 10 b. Visual Studio Build Tools 2017 (which nobody really mentions that you need, it's free from Microsoft)
b1. Visual C++ 2014, which may come as part of the Visual Studio Build Tools, I'm not sure. I installed the Visual C++ Redistributable and things didn't work, but did after installing the Build Tools using the Visual Studio Installer from Microsoft. c. CUDA 9.0 (not 9.1) d. Cudnn 7.0 (not 7.1, and you need the version for CUDA 9.0, not CUDA 9.1) e. Cmake 3.10 - I'm pretty sure this fixed one of the errors, but I put so much stuff on my machine today I can't remember for sure. 3. Getting the "pip install -r requirements.txt" command took a bit of doing - Faceswap doesn't have a file called "requirements.txt", it's called "requirements-gpu-python36-cuda9.txt". It's easier to rename this to something shorter, because I had to run it about 20 times before everything worked. 4. I found that using absolute paths for things (e.g. entering the path as c:\faceswap\faceset\model_A instead of a relative path). You'll be typing a lot of paths, so use short folder and file names. 5. I have a Geforce 1050 Ti video card and spent half a day trying to figure out why the training ran once and not again. Turns out using the LowMem option worked, even though it says it's for cards with <2GB. NOTE: If you use LowMem for the training, you need to use LowMem for the converting too.

Hope this helps,
